FLAGSHIP CASE SIMULATION

Should We Invest in Solar? (Cape Manufacturing)

Compare three proposals and defend a recommendation.

DURATION

65–80 minute interactive case

Self-paced learning with a working spreadsheet model.

TECHNICAL ENVIRONMENT

Microsoft Excel & Google Sheets

Spreadsheet essentials are included.

01 / WHAT THE CASE TESTS

FROM OPERATOR TO ADVISER

Technical output.
Human judgement.
01

COMMON PITFALL

Untraceable inputs.

Retyped inputs obscure the assumptions behind a result.

IN THIS CASE

Traceable formulas.

Link calculations to Case Data!A3:F17 and inspect broken references.

02

COMMON PITFALL

One metric decides.

Payback and long-term value can favour different proposals.

IN THIS CASE

Competing criteria.

A has the shortest payback (2.92 years); C has the highest base-case NPV (R2.871m).

03

COMMON PITFALL

Claims without evidence.

Annual averages hide when electricity is actually used.

IN THIS CASE

Operational evidence.

Check half-hourly load profiles and seek independent evidence for environmental claims.

02 / THE CURRICULUM

A FICTIONAL INVESTMENT CASE

One case.
One decision.

Take the seat of a commercial analyst advising the Financial Director. Compare three rooftop solar proposals costing R650,000 to R990,000.

65–80 MINUTES
SIX MODULES
A WORKING SPREADSHEET MODEL

Cape Manufacturing fictional case. Base-case proposal data; tariff R2.80 per kWh.
Case data	Proposal A	Proposal B	Proposal C
Investment	R650,000	R820,000	R990,000
System size	60 kWp	80 kWp	100 kWp
Self-consumption	90%	85%	78%
Simple payback	2.92 years	2.96 years	3.22 years
20-year NPV	R2.152m	R2.662m	R2.871m

ILLUSTRATIVE CASE DATA / CASE DATA!A3:F17 / FIGURES ARE NOT AN INVESTMENT RECOMMENDATION.

MODULE 01 / 06 — INTERPRET THE INPUTS & SELF-CONSUMPTION BRIDGE

Understand

FOUNDATIONAL COMPETENCE

FD / MONDAY 09:00 · FINANCIAL DIRECTOR

“First, establish what we are buying—and what we can use.”

Check the proposal data before calculating. A larger system produces more electricity, but how much of that output will actually reduce our grid purchases?

Before entering a single formula, participants record an explicit initial prediction and examine why gross technical output (147,000 kWh for System C) does not automatically translate into economic value when unused electricity earns zero revenue.

Analytical & spreadsheet mechanics
Behavioural & judgement shift

OBSERVABLE WORKBOOK EVIDENCE

Recorded pre-model metric prediction + concept-check explanation of why neither gross generation nor self-consumption alone identifies the best investment.
